questions.q: What did Langer's counterclockwise study find?
a: Men who lived as if younger showed better memory and strength
Older men declined faster when placed in a new setting
The retreat had no measurable effect on the men's health
Only the youngest participants showed any improvement
questions.why: The overview describes 80-year-old men at a retreat styled as 20 years earlier whose memory, vision and strength improved.

questions.q: Why does Langer say a medical diagnosis is never complete?
a: It is based on statistical averages, not your whole condition
Doctors rarely take the time to study symptoms
Medical tests are usually inaccurate
Patients hide most of their symptoms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a label like bronchitis comes from an average, so part of your personal condition falls outside it.

questions.q: How does the word remission affect cancer survivors, according to Langer?
a: It suggests the disease is only waiting to return
It makes them feel permanently cured
It has no effect on how they feel
It encourages them to stop treatment early
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts remission with cured and links the label a patient adopts to her overall well-being.

questions.q: Why can doctors' uniforms be a problem?
a: They push doctor and patient into rigid, mindless roles
They spread infection between patients
They intimidate patients into paying more
They make doctors seem less qualified
questions.why: The summary says formal uniforms reinforce a script that makes both sides act mindlessly, without attention.

questions.q: What is the core of mindful health, as Langer describes it?
a: Paying attention to how your symptoms vary moment to moment
Following your treatment plan without asking questions
Meditating for an hour every morning
Tracking only whether you feel healthy or ill
questions.why: Lesson 3 says mindful health means noticing variability on a continuum instead of thinking in healthy-or-ill terms.
